name: Plus 15 Skywalk Network
description: Explore downtown above the streets on Calgary’s weather-protected skywalk network, linking towers, shops, hotels, and public spaces.
personalNote: Use the network as a route between downtown stops; individual bridges and building hours can vary.

name: Calgary Tower
description: Rise above downtown for sweeping city views from Calgary’s iconic tower lookout.
personalNote: A useful orientation point for a first visit to Calgary.

name: Stephen Avenue Walk
description: Walk Calgary’s historic main street past sandstone façades, local shops, inviting restaurants, and colourful public art.
personalNote: Pairs naturally with the Calgary Tower and CORE shopping centre.

name: The Bow and Wonderland
description: Marvel at Calgary’s striking Bow tower and step beneath Wonderland, the giant sculpture welcoming visitors at its base.
personalNote: A quick stop that works well as part of a downtown walking route.

name: Calgary Central Library
description: Step inside Calgary’s award-winning Central Library, a dramatic modern landmark built for discovery and design.
personalNote: Allow time to walk through the building rather than viewing it only from outside.

name: Studio Bell, home of the National Music Centre
description: Dive into Canada’s musical story through immersive exhibits, rare instruments, and live performances at Studio Bell.
personalNote: Combine it with the Central Library and an onward walk toward Inglewood.

name: Inglewood Main Street
description: Walk Calgary’s oldest neighbourhood for local craft breweries, independent boutiques, galleries, and character-filled restaurants.
personalNote: Best treated as a flexible wandering stop rather than one fixed attraction.

name: Peace Bridge
description: Cross Calgary’s iconic Peace Bridge for striking architecture, river views, and an easy connection to downtown pathways.
personalNote: Particularly photogenic in the evening and easy to pair with the RiverWalk.
address: Peace Bridge, Bow River Path (North), Calgary, AB
bestTime: Evening in summer; daylight in winter

name: Prince’s Island Park
description: Escape into a leafy Bow River island with winding paths, open lawns, and lively seasonal events.
personalNote: A good reset between downtown sightseeing stops.
bestTime: Summer evening or any clear day

name: Heritage Park Historical Village
description: Step into Alberta’s past at a sprawling living-history village filled with heritage buildings, hands-on demonstrations, and old-fashioned fun.
personalNote: Plan for at least half a day and check the operating calendar before going.

name: Bowness Park
description: Spend a relaxed day beside the lagoon at this beloved west Calgary park, with scenic paths and year-round recreation.
personalNote: Summer boating and winter skating give the park very different personalities.

name: Fish Creek Provincial Park
description: Wander through Calgary’s wild side on miles of trails winding through forests, meadows, and a beautiful river valley.
personalNote: Choose a specific entrance or trailhead before visiting; the park is very large.
address: Fish Creek Provincial Park, Calgary, AB

name: Fish Creek Provincial Park — East Entrance
description: Enter Fish Creek’s eastern reaches for forested paths, creek-valley scenery, and a quieter route into Calgary’s natural playground.
personalNote: Use this east-side entrance when exploring the park from Bow Bottom Trail; conditions and access can vary by season.
address: Bow Valley Ranch, 15975 Bow Bottom Trail SE, Calgary, AB

name: The Family of Man
description: Pause beneath The Family of Man, a landmark downtown sculpture with a story woven into Calgary’s public art scene.
personalNote: A quick public-art stop near The Bow and Stephen Avenue.

name: 10th & 10th Mural
description: Find a bold, large-scale mural brightening the corner of 10 Avenue and 10 Street SW.
personalNote: Pin the mural itself rather than treating the whole block as the destination.
address: First on Tenth, 123 10 Avenue SW, Calgary, AB

name: CORE Shopping Centre and Devonian Gardens
description: Shop, stroll, and discover a lush indoor garden oasis at the heart of downtown.
personalNote: A useful indoor stop in winter and a natural Plus 15 connection.

name: Devonian Gardens
description: Find a tropical escape downtown among Devonian Gardens’ greenery, winding paths, and bright indoor calm.
personalNote: Especially useful as a warm, quiet break during a downtown walk.

name: Eighth Avenue Place
description: Admire sleek downtown architecture and public art while passing through one of the Plus 15 network’s polished hubs.
personalNote: Use it as a Plus 15 connection from CORE; has a Starbucks.

name: Udderly Art Pasture
description: Meet Calgary’s playful side through a colourful herd of decorated cow sculptures in this memorable public-art installation.
personalNote: The current legacy display is associated with Centennial Parkade; confirm the display before visiting.

name: 17th Avenue SW
description: Follow Calgary’s lively social strip for buzzing patios, standout restaurants, late-night bars, and independent shops.
personalNote: Best explored as a flexible evening stroll rather than a single stop.
address: 17 Avenue SW and 8 Street SW, Calgary, AB
bestTime: Evening for nightlife; daytime for shopping

name: BUMP Mural Project — World’s Tallest Mural
description: Look up at DAIM’s towering BUMP mural, a dramatic piece of Calgary street art stretching across First on Tenth.
personalNote: Pinned to First on Tenth at 123 10 Avenue SW, the location of the world’s-tallest-mural project.
address: First on Tenth, 123 10 Avenue SW, Calgary, AB

name: Lougheed House
description: Tour an elegant sandstone mansion surrounded by gardens and stories from Calgary’s early high society.
personalNote: A calmer contrast to the restaurants and nightlife of 17th Avenue.

name: The Confluence Historic Site and Parkland
description: Stand where Calgary’s rivers and history meet, with open parkland marking the city’s earliest beginnings.
personalNote: The site is the modern successor to the Fort Calgary location and redevelopment.

name: St. Patrick’s Island
description: Explore a beautifully renewed Bow River island with playful landscapes, open lawns, and direct access to RiverWalk.
personalNote: A natural extension of an East Village and RiverWalk outing.

name: Esker Foundation
description: Encounter bold, ever-changing contemporary art from Canadian and international artists in an intimate gallery setting.
personalNote: Check the current exhibition and hours before building it into a route.

name: Cold Garden Beverage Company
description: Raise a glass at a bright, creative neighbourhood brewery pouring colourful craft beers and good-time energy.
personalNote: A good brewery stop when extending the Inglewood walk south and east.

name: Crescent Heights Lookout / McHugh Bluff
description: Climb to this bluff-top lookout for one of Calgary’s most spectacular skyline panoramas.
personalNote: One of the strongest skyline viewpoints in the city; allow time for the stairs.
bestTime: Evening in summer; daylight in winter

name: Eau Claire Plaza
description: Unwind beside the Bow at this welcoming riverside plaza, a scenic gateway to Calgary’s downtown pathways.
personalNote: Check current construction and access conditions before visiting.

name: RiverWalk — West Side
description: Follow the Bow River west through peaceful pathways, open skies, and easy connections to Eau Claire, Prince’s Island, and Peace Bridge.
personalNote: Connect it with Eau Claire, Prince’s Island Park, and Peace Bridge.

name: Gasoline Alley Museum
description: Get close to gleaming vintage cars, remarkable machines, and the stories that powered Alberta’s transportation history.
personalNote: It is included with Heritage Park admission and is worth allowing extra time for.

name: Baker Park
description: Slow down beside the Bow at a peaceful riverside park with open lawns, scenic paths, and room to breathe.
personalNote: A natural pairing with Bowness Park, although they are not the same park.

name: Nose Hill Park
description: Hike across Calgary’s wide-open prairie landscape for winding trails, wild horizons, and sweeping city views.
personalNote: Choose a trailhead before visiting because the park has many entrances.

name: Inglewood Bird Sanctuary
description: Spot birds and wildlife along quiet trails in this protected Elbow River sanctuary, a hidden nature retreat in the city.
personalNote: A quieter alternative to the busier Inglewood commercial strip.

name: North Glenmore Park
description: Enjoy big skies, reservoir views, and unhurried walks through one of Calgary’s favourite lakeside parks.
personalNote: Good for a slower walk, especially when paired with Glenmore Reservoir activities.

name: Bow River Rafting from Edworthy Park
description: Float into summer on a refreshing Bow River adventure, drifting from Edworthy Park beneath Calgary’s open skies.
personalNote: Use a current outfitter and check water conditions; this is weather- and season-dependent.

name: Calgary Zoo
description: Meet fascinating animals, explore beautiful gardens, and fill a day with discovery at one of Canada’s top city zoos.
personalNote: Arrive early for a more comfortable visit and better animal activity.

name: WinSport / Canada Olympic Park
description: Turn up the adventure at Calgary’s Olympic legacy park with thrilling year-round activities and mountain-facing views.
personalNote: Downhill karting and other activities are seasonal; check the current calendar.
address: 88 Canada Olympic Road SW, Calgary, AB

name: Cobb’s Adventure Park
description: Let the whole family loose at a seasonal adventure park packed with playful outdoor activities.
personalNote: Confirm the current opening dates and activities before visiting.

name: SAM Centre and Calgary Stampede Grounds
description: Get behind the scenes of Calgary’s western spirit through an interactive Stampede experience on the historic grounds.
personalNote: Check whether the Stampede itself is operating before planning a grounds visit.
address: 1911 Big Four Trail SE, Calgary, AB
bestTime: Daytime; check hours and event dates

name: The Hangar Flight Museum
description: Step among remarkable aircraft and uncover Canada’s aviation, military, and transportation stories.
personalNote: A good indoor option and an easy pairing with the Calgary Zoo area.

name: TELUS Spark Science Centre
description: Spark your curiosity with hands-on experiments, immersive shows, and star-filled planetarium journeys.
personalNote: Allow several hours if visiting with children; check special programming in advance.
address: 220 St. George’s Drive NE, Calgary, AB
